newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine parliament tries to speed '97 budget bill.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine parliament tries to speed '97 budget bill.

text.p: Ukraine's parliament, trying to speed long-delayed work on this year's draft budget, on Friday told two commissions working on the bill to solve outstanding issues by Tuesday in the hope of passing it next week.
Deputies debated the bill in general on Friday and are due to consider it article by article on June 24, about six months after it was given its first reading.

The deputies approved a decision read out by speaker Olexander Moroz to ask a temporary commission trying to speed up the budget process and the budget commission to work out problems by Tuesday "so as to pass the budget next week".
Budget approval is a key item on a list of 41 conditions Ukraine must meet to qualify for a $2.4-$3 billion Extended Fund Facility loan from the International Monetary Fund (IMF).
Stanley Fischer, the Fund's deputy managing director, met President Leonid Kuchma on Thursday and was due to meet him again on Friday.

A deputy economy minister said on Wednesday that 27 of the conditions had been fulfilled and the Fund had agreed to delay some of them by several months, including cancellation of export taxes on livestock and leather and pension reform.
